title: Prime localizations of tame cyclotomic integer rings are fields or DVRs
statement: Let $N\geq1$ be an integer and $\zeta\in\mathbf C$ a primitive $N$th root of unity, meaning that $\zeta^N=1$ and $\zeta^j\neq1$ for $0<j<N$. Let $A=\mathbf Z[1/N,\zeta]\subset\mathbf C$ be the subring generated by the integers, $1/N$ and $\zeta$. For every prime ideal $\mathfrak p$ of $A$, the localization $A_{\mathfrak p}$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime] is either a field or a discrete valuation ring [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring].

source.place: Tag 0AP2 (lemma-Dedekind-etale-extension), applied to the cyclotomic factor of Z[1/N][T]/(T^N-1); the coefficient ring is the one in Expose X 1.2--1.3 of Travaux de Gabber. Cyclotomic-factor identification and the zero-prime field case are part of this auxiliary arithmetic statement.

proof.text: Put $R=\mathbf Z[1/N]\subset\mathbf C$. Since $N\geq1$, its powers are nonzero, and the fraction map $a/N^k\mapsto a/N^k$ embeds this localization in $\mathbf C$. By [lem-weil-pbc-z-localizations-dvr], $\mathbf Z$ is Noetherian and integrally closed with dimension one. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-localization-noetherian] and [lem-weil-pbc-localization-normal-domain] to the powers of $N$: $R$ is a Noetherian integrally closed domain. Clause (1) of [lem-weil-pbc-localization-prime-residue-field-iso] identifies its primes with the primes of $\mathbf Z$ disjoint from these powers. This bijection and its inverse (extension of ideals) preserve inclusion, so strict chains remain strict and $\dim R\leq1$.

Set $B=R[T]/(T^N-1)$ and let $t$ denote the class of $T$. Apply [lem-sfb-unit-binomial-finite-etale] with $n=N$ and $u=1$. Its unit hypotheses hold because $1/N\in R$. It gives the $R$-basis $1,t,\ldots,t^{N-1}$ and an etale morphism $\operatorname{Spec}B\to\operatorname{Spec}R$. Evaluation $t\mapsto\zeta$ defines a surjective $R$-algebra map $e:B\to A$: the relation holds since $\zeta^N=1$, and the image is exactly the subring generated by $R$ and $\zeta$. The images $1,\zeta,\ldots,\zeta^{N-1}$ therefore generate $A$ as an $R$-module. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-algebra-noetherian] separately to $B$ and $A$; both are Noetherian.

source.place: Tag 03PL (lemma-kummer-sequence), proof: the unit-root algebra is finite free and etale; Noetherianity is Algebra Tag 00FN (lemma-Noetherian-permanence).

proof.text: For each prime $\mathfrak r\subset R$, [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-stalk-localization](c), applied to the whole affine scheme, identifies the stalk of $\operatorname{Spec}R$ with $R_{\mathfrak r}$. These are integrally closed domains by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-normal-domain], applied now to $R$ and $R\setminus\mathfrak r$. Thus $\operatorname{Spec}R$ has normal domain stalks. The etale morphism of step 2 is smooth by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-smooth-zero-dimensional-fibres]. Apply [lem-sfb-smooth-normal-ascent] to this morphism: every stalk of $\operatorname{Spec}B$ is an integrally closed domain.

source.place: Tag 034F (lemma-normal-local-smooth), ascent; with Schemes Tag 01HV (lemma-spec-sheaves), Algebra Tag 00GY, and Morphisms Tag 02GK (lemma-etale-smooth-unramified).

proof.text: Take $X=\operatorname{Spec}B$ and $U=X$. Since $B$ is Noetherian, its single affine chart makes $X$ locally Noetherian by [pqf-def-locnoeth]. It is quasi-compact by [lem-weil-pbc-spec-basic-opens-unit-ideal-quasi-compact](iii). The stalk hypothesis was proved in step 3. Hence [lem-sbc-normal-sections-finite-product] supplies a finite product of integrally closed domains $D_i$ and an isomorphism $B\simeq\prod_{i=1}^sD_i$, using the global-sections identification in [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Give each $D_i$ its $R$-algebra structure by composing $R\to B$ with this isomorphism and the projection. Each projection $B\to D_i$ is surjective, so the projections of the $N$ module generators of $B$ generate $D_i$ over $R$.

View $e$ as a surjection $\prod_iD_i\to A$ using step 4. The ring $A\subset\mathbf C$ is a nonzero domain. The coordinate idempotents have pairwise zero products and sum to $1$, and their images in a domain are $0$ or $1$; exactly one image is $1$. In particular $s\ne0$. If its index is $i$, all other coordinate summands are killed, so $e$ factors through a surjective $R$-algebra map $h:D_i\to A$. Write $\mathfrak q=\ker h$; this is prime since $A$ is a domain.

source.place: Tag 00ED (lemma-spec-product), the coordinate-idempotent argument, written explicitly here.

proof.text: The finite $R$-module $D_i$ of step 4 is integral over $R$ by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-algebra-is-integral]. The map $R\to D_i$ is injective because its composite with $h$ is the inclusion $R\subset A\subset\mathbf C$. Consequently the prime ideals $(0)\subseteq\mathfrak q$ of the domain $D_i$ both contract to $(0)$ in $R$: for $\mathfrak q$ this follows from the same injective composite. Apply [pqf-lem-incomparability] to these comparable primes of the integral extension $R\to D_i$. It yields $\mathfrak q=(0)$. Thus $h$ is an isomorphism, and $A$ is integrally closed because $D_i$ is. This identifies the actual evaluation image with a normal component, rather than assuming that a quotient of a normal ring is normal.

source.place: Tags 00GK (lemma-finite-is-integral) and 00GT (lemma-integral-no-inclusion), the latter used for the two primes (0) and ker h.

proof.text: The finite $R$-module $A$ of step 2 is integral over $R$ by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-algebra-is-integral]. By [pqf-lem-incomparability], contraction of any strict chain of prime ideals of $A$ is a strict chain in $R$. Since $\dim R\leq1$, it follows that $\dim A\leq1$. Now suppose $\mathfrak p\ne(0)$. The chain $(0)\subsetneq\mathfrak p$ forces $\dim A=1$, and any prime strictly above $\mathfrak p$ would give a chain of length two. Thus $\mathfrak p$ is maximal. Together with steps 2 and 6, $A$ is a Noetherian integrally closed domain of dimension one. Apply [lem-sc-dedekind-localization-dvr] to $A$ and this maximal ideal to obtain that $A_{\mathfrak p}$ is a discrete valuation ring.

source.place: Tags 00GK (lemma-finite-is-integral), 00GT (lemma-integral-no-inclusion), and 034X (lemma-characterize-Dedekind), implication (3) to (2), at a nonzero maximal ideal.

proof.text: If $\mathfrak p=(0)$, [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime] inverts every nonzero element of the domain $A$. A nonzero fraction $a/s$ has $a\ne0$ (the fraction equality and the domain property give this), and its inverse is $s/a$. The fractions $0/1$ and $1/1$ are distinct because $A\subset\mathbf C$ is nonzero. Thus $A_{(0)}$ is a field. Together with step 7 this proves the required alternative for every prime, including $N=1$.

Shape: one commit with the item and its report. No new nodes. Statement, stmt_deps, source and blueprint are retained, with same_as []. There is no repair note for this item and no SGA citation. Reachability: in weil-newtargets the item is live (citer lem-per-local-cyclotomic-group-algebra-split; its citer closure reaches the nt-target nodes), so the dropped-route RETURN of Q27 67af does not apply here. Source: Stacks more-algebra Tag 0AP2, lines 10880-10898. The delivery follows its normal-component route instead of 0AP2's dimension/regularity lemmas, with proof_origin by=agent. Step 1: R=Z[1/N] is a Noetherian normal domain of dimension at most 1, by z-localizations-dvr, localization-noetherian, localization-normal-domain (0 is not in S) and prime-residue (1), which gives an inclusion-preserving bijection. Step 2: unit-binomial with n=N, u=1 (N is a unit in R) gives a free basis and an etale map. Evaluation t to zeta is well defined and maps onto A, so A is a finite R-module, and both B and A are Noetherian. Step 3: affine-open-stalk (c) gives O_{Spec R,r} = R_r, which is a normal domain. etale-smooth says f is smooth, and smooth-normal-ascent then gives normal domain stalks on Spec B with no extra hypotheses. Step 4: Spec B is locally Noetherian with one chart and quasi-compact by spec-basic-opens (iii); normal-sections-finite-product gives B = prod D_i. Each D_i is a finite R-module because the generators project onto it; the step proves this itself, not from the node. Step 5: the orthogonal idempotents of the product map into the domain A, so exactly one goes to 1. Hence s is at least 1 and e factors as h: D_i onto A. Step 6: R to D_i is injective because its composite with h is the inclusion of R in A. So (0) and ker h both contract to 0, and incomparability gives ker h = 0. Thus D_i is A and A is integrally closed. Step 7: incomparability gives dim A at most dim R, which is at most 1. A nonzero p forces dim A = 1 and p maximal, and the Dedekind-localization node then gives a DVR in the sense of def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring. Step 8: the zero prime gives the fraction field. Edge cases checked: N=1 (R=A=Z, B=R), N=2, N=6 (not a prime power), and the zero prime. Primitivity is unused, which does not weaken the statement. Duplicate search: the 0AP2 nodes lem-sbc-etale-trait-stalk and lem-sfb-etale-dvr-principal-neighbourhood work over a DVR base and do not state the item, and no Dedekind-plus-etale node states it.
